item.title: Ansem’s wallet was drained. The advice was restraint
item.description: A wallet tied to the trader behind $ANSEM was drained on Tuesday. Prominent SPX6900 voices asked the crowd not to gloat.
item.content:encoded:
A wallet tied to the trader behind $ANSEM was drained on Tuesday. Prominent SPX6900 voices asked the crowd not to gloat.

Early on Tuesday, 24 November, the trader @blknoiz06, known as Ansem, posted that his "pump wallet is hacked." He said he believed someone had got into his Bullpen profile, where a Solana private key had been imported. Later that morning @BullpenFi said it had found unauthorized transfers involving 18 to 19 accounts opened during its early beta, between April and June 2024, his among them. By the evening the company said it was working with the FBI and other authorities to trace and freeze the funds. Who was behind it had not been made public.

Ansem's name is attached to $ANSEM, a Solana memecoin. In the week before, some SPX6900 posters had held it up as a contrast to their own token. On Tuesday the louder response from the same crowd was a request to stop. @1d34h4z4rd quoted Proverbs 24:17, "Do not rejoice when your enemies fall," and called grave dancing "an ersatz victory." Replying, @6400more wrote that "Ansem holders are in a lot of pain and we should open our hearts to them," and signed off: "Be kind aeons." Shortly after, @MustStopMurad posted: "We don't need to attack others while they are down. We just need to persist with our own cause." He named no one.

Not everyone took the note. @matuaxbt objected to Murad "making Ansem a victim." Others treated the day as a recruiting opportunity: @realthigh told the token's holders, "you have a home at spx6900." Bullpen says the incident is still under investigation.

item.title: They call themselves Aeons
item.description: The name arrived with a secret NFT mint in November 2023. Community pages say it means eternity. The dictionary, and the paper trail, are a little more complicated.
item.content:encoded:
The name arrived with a secret NFT mint in November 2023. Community pages say it means eternity. The dictionary, and the paper trail, are a little more complicated.

People who hold SPX6900, or who want to be counted among them, call themselves Aeons. The project site uses the word the same way. So do the Sunday Spaces, the meetups, and the greetings at the end of posts. It is the crowd's name for itself. How it got there is less settled than the name is now.

In ordinary English, an aeon is a very long age. The spelling is the Commonwealth one; Americans usually write eon. Dictionaries trace it through Latin aeon to the Greek αἰών (aiōn), a word that started as a lifetime and came to mean an age, an era, or eternity. A community about page at aeons6900.com puts it more simply, and a little short of that path: Aeon, it says, is "the name people give to those holding SPX token, it means eternity in ancient latin." Latin did borrow the word, and Late Latin used it for age and eternity. The root is Greek. The same dictionaries also record a Gnostic sense, a spirit being emanating from the Godhead. No official post or project page cited here uses that meaning as the source of this name.

What the public record does show is a date. On 16 November 2023, the official @spx6900 account presented "our first secret project reveal: Project Aeon," a collection of 3,333 pieces: 1,111 free mints, 1,111 discount mints, and 1,111 public, the first two limited to a snapshot. A community timeline on that same about page dates the launch to 15 November, which lines up with the same evening in North America. A few hours later the official account said the collection had minted out. The lore written around those tokens is science fiction, not scripture: a fictional "quantum glitch" at SPX6900 Labs that sparked 3,333 beings "neither of this world nor wholly apart from it," as the collection's story tells it. The official links page calls them "3,333 divine beings." The commandments page later describes aeons as "our custom on-chain identities," the line of mascots after Marie Rose.

Who chose the word is not a matter of a single signed claim. A later official post, in July 2026, called the collection "a community-driven secret project under the creative direction of @PankoPunk, delivered in November 2023 to provide a visual identity to SPX6900." On the night it minted out, the same official account thanked @baka_console and asked people to reply "Thank You Denko!" Those are credits for the work. They are not, on their own, a statement of who first said the holders should be called Aeons. A search of public posts from the token's August 2023 launch until the mint did not turn up the word being used as a name for the crowd. That does not prove nobody said it in a chat or a Space. It does mean the paper trail on X starts with the collection.

The jump from token to people was quick. By late December 2023 the official account was addressing the crowd in the singular, as if the word were already a greeting: "buckle up, aeon." "ily aeon" and "ily aeons," a shorthand for "I love you," show up in community posts within days of the mint. A later Reddit glossary treats Aeon as both a devoted member and a holder of one of the 3,333 tokens, and lists "Ilyaeon" as the same affection written as one word. The two senses were not kept apart. The picture became a profile. The profile became a person.

The rest of the vocabulary hung off that name. Cognisphere, on the community about page, is "the shared consciousness where Aeons Plug themselves to form One Unique Entity." The official about page puts it in the project's own voice: "The risk averse are rejected by Lumina at Cognisphere's Gate, we march with full conviction." By early 2024 the official account was telling people to enter the cognisphere, and the Project Aeon account used the same line to open a Discord. A poetic style of self-description, "Aeon of the SPX6900 Cognisphere," is still in circulation. Event names followed the root: Mondaeon for a regular Monday call, CarolinAeon for a gathering in South Carolina. Persist forever, a slogan the official commandments page traces to a remark by RaoulGMI, is tied on the community about page to the idea that Aeons already means eternity. Those are two accounts of the same phrase. They can sit beside each other.

Flip the stock market is the mission the name is supposed to outlast. The word does two jobs at once, which is probably why it stuck. It is a character you can put on, and a claim that you mean to stay for a long time. Whether that is a lifetime, an age, or eternity depends on which page you are reading. This is a retelling for a community site. It is not an offer, and nothing here is a reason to buy a token or a picture of one.

item.title: Volleyball practice, volume 24
item.description: Sunday’s recurring SPX6900 Space went ahead as scheduled. A recording of Murad’s monologue followed.
item.content:encoded:
Sunday’s recurring SPX6900 Space went ahead as scheduled. A recording of Murad’s monologue followed.

On Sunday afternoon, @MustStopMurad posted the live link for a recurring X Space the community calls Volleyball Practice. This one was volume 24. He had flagged it the night before as "Why Tokenized Movements are the Future of Crypto," set for 2 p.m. Eastern, 7 p.m. UTC, on 22 November.

@KennyCrypto6900, writing while the Space was on, said there were "hundreds of aeons" in the room "at the stone cold bottom." That headcount has not been confirmed by the host, and X’s own attendance figures were not public after the fact. @cryptonut100, who had earlier pointed people to an 11 a.m. Pacific start, later wrote that the token "doesn’t get its legitimacy from Wall Street, the media, or anyone’s permission," but from "regular people deciding together to treat it like it’s real." That is one listener’s reading, not a finding.

After the Space ended, @leongaban posted a recording of Murad’s monologue from the session, and a copy on YouTube under the title "Murad on SPX 6900 - Sunday’s SPX Volley ball space." The official @spx6900 account did not post about the gathering. Nothing said in the room is advice from this page.

item.title: How SPX6900 started
item.description: A fair launch on Ethereum in August 2023, a crew that left, and a crowd that kept the joke until it had a name.
item.content:encoded:
A fair launch on Ethereum in August 2023, a crew that left, and a crowd that kept the joke until it had a name.

In August 2023 a token named SPX6900 showed up on Ethereum. The launch the project still describes was a fair launch. Liquidity was locked for 69 years, out to 2092, and then the people who started it left. The about page on spx6900.com uses one word for that status: vanished. The contract was renounced. A slice of the supply was burned. What remained was the ticker, and whoever felt like repeating it.

The name is a pun with a ruler in it. SPX is the ticker people already use for the S&P 500. 6900 is a bigger number than 500, and 69 is the number the internet will not leave alone. Put them together and the inequality writes itself: 6900 beats 500. The token does not hold those five hundred companies, track that index, or answer to S&P Dow Jones Indices. The project site says so. It also says the token has no intrinsic value and no expected financial return.

The supply figures on that page are round on purpose. One billion tokens at the maximum. Burned: 69,006,909, which is 6.90 percent. Circulating: 930,993,091. Holders took what was left and gave themselves a name. Aeons. There is no company to write to. The posters, the meetups, and the timelines are the institution.

Two sentences did most of the recruiting. Stop trading and believe in something. Flip the stock market. By early 2025 they were traveling as a pair, on avatars and on the front door of the project site. The crowd’s target, said with a straight face, is 69 trillion dollars. Anything between here and there they call weather. The only question they allow is whether the stock market has been flipped. The answer they stamp is still no. There is no chart.

Home is still the Ethereum contract. The project site lists bridged copies on Solana, Base, BNB Chain, and Sui, and it warns that a bridge can fail on its own even when the story does not. Later, a public advocate named Murad, @MustStopMurad, started telling the story in long interviews: a belief system, a movement coin, a thesis with a pile of reasons. He is not the vanished launcher. He showed up after the crew was already gone and argued that the joke was the product.

This is a retelling for a community site. It is not an offer, not a forecast, and not a reason to buy anything. Confirm the contracts on spx6900.com before you trust a token with this name. Copycats reuse it.

item.title: Murad did not launch it
item.description: The interviews on this site are from the advocate who showed up later, not from the crew that vanished.
item.content:encoded:
The interviews on this site are from the advocate who showed up later, not from the crew that vanished.

Search the name Murad next to SPX6900 and the interviews arrive first. That is recent history. The token’s own timeline starts in August 2023, with a fair launch and a crew the project site now calls vanished. Murad, @MustStopMurad, is a later public voice. He argues for the bit on other people’s shows. He did not renounce the contract, lock the liquidity, or burn the supply.

The videos filed here are those conversations: NGMI, The Block, Southern Fried Chad, and threadguy. They are worth hearing if you want the case in his words. They are not the founding documents, and nothing said in them is advice from this page. The line he repeats, stop trading and believe in something, was already the crowd’s line.

If a clip names a price, treat it as weather. The stamp on the front of this site is still no.

item.title: Two sentences did the recruiting
item.description: Stop trading and believe in something. Flip the stock market. By early 2025 the pair was doing the work.
item.content:encoded:
Stop trading and believe in something. Flip the stock market. By early 2025 the pair was doing the work.

Most of what outsiders can repeat about SPX6900 fits in two lines. Stop trading and believe in something. Flip the stock market. They showed up together in public posts by early 2025, then on avatars, merch, and the front of spx6900.com.

The first line is a refusal of the usual routine: the next ticker, the next chart, the next hour. The second line is the goal they say with a straight face. Together they are the recruiting poster. The rest of the lore hangs off them.

Neither line is a promise of a return. They are the joke, said often enough that a crowd started answering to it.

item.title: Ethereum is still home
item.description: Copies on Solana, Base, BNB Chain, and Sui are bridges. A bridge can fail on its own.
item.content:encoded:
Copies on Solana, Base, BNB Chain, and Sui are bridges. A bridge can fail on its own.

The token people mean when they say SPX6900 started on Ethereum. The project site also lists copies on Solana, Base, BNB Chain, and Sui. Those are bridged. The site’s own warning is that a bridge can fail even when the story does not.

The comfortable contract, in the project’s words, is the Ethereum one. The five addresses, and the supply figures printed beside them, are on the learn page here and on spx6900.com. Compare them there. The name gets reused by copycats.

This is a map, not a reason to buy. Money put into the token can go to zero.
